name: Starlink V2 Mini (on-station, brightness-mitigated)
note: Benchmark model for Mallama et al. 2023 (mallama2023_v2mini): V2 Minis in SpaceX's on-station mitigation conops. Body frame: +Z nadir, +X velocity, +Y = +Z x +X. Nadir face under the gen-2 dielectric mirror film, the rest of the bus black; arrays track the Sun but never tip their plane below the Earth's limb. Orbit raising, station-keeping burns and deorbit (unmitigated, ~5 at 1000 km) are not modelled.

sources.subject: bus
sources.value: 4.1 x 2.7 x 0.4 m flat bus, nadir-pointing, +X along velocity; black paint
sources.source: McDowell, planet4589.org/astro/starsim (V2 Mini: bus 4.1 x 2.7 m, solar array 4.1 x 12.8 m per wing); thickness and the velocity-aligned yaw are estimates. SpaceX, 'Brightness Mitigation Best Practices for Satellite Operators' (2022, starlink.com/public-files/BrightnessMitigationBestPracticesSatelliteOperators.pdf): 'black paint for components with complex geometries' ('Low Reflectivity Black'); the whole non-nadir bus uses it here.

sources.subject: nadir_mirror_film
sources.value: second-generation dielectric mirror film over the nadir face
sources.source: SpaceX, 'Brightness Mitigation Best Practices for Satellite Operators' (2022, starlink.com/public-files/BrightnessMitigationBestPracticesSatelliteOperators.pdf): 'SpaceX covers the bottom of its satellites with a second-generation dielectric mirror film' and 'will orient the flat satellite nadir surface so that the specular peak never intersects Earth'. Film reflectance: the dielectric_mirror_gen2 preset (estimate).

sources.subject: wings
sources.value: both arrays on one cross-track hinge, tracking the Sun but held within 22 deg of zenith
sources.source: Mallama, Cole, Harrington & Maley 2023 (arXiv:2306.06657) section 5 (SpaceX private communication): 'Gen 2 Starlinks place the solar arrays edge-on to the Earth's limb so observers on the ground will not usually see portions of the solar array that are illuminated by the Sun'; SpaceX, 'Brightness Mitigation Best Practices for Satellite Operators' (2022, starlink.com/public-files/BrightnessMitigationBestPracticesSatelliteOperators.pdf): 'terminator tracking ... will point the knife edge of the solar array at the earth limb' with a 25% power cost. DERIVED: an array plane tilted at most 90 - rho from zenith (rho = Earth's angular radius, 66.7-68.4 deg at 480-560 km) keeps the whole Earth behind it. SpaceX does this only near the terminator; away from it the arrays track fully, but a satellite is only seen from the night side near the terminator, so the clamp is applied always.

sources.value: two 4.1 x 12.8 m arrays; dark inter-cell cells, opaque dark backsheet
sources.source: McDowell, planet4589.org/astro/starsim (V2 Mini: bus 4.1 x 2.7 m, solar array 4.1 x 12.8 m per wing). SpaceX, 'Brightness Mitigation Best Practices for Satellite Operators' (2022, starlink.com/public-files/BrightnessMitigationBestPracticesSatelliteOperators.pdf): 'an opaque pigment for the solar backsheet'. Backsheet reflectance: the array_backsheet_dark preset (estimate). 0.5 m boom gap: estimate.
